title: Time Jump — 07:40, Hospital on Paper for Four Hours

fields.narration: Facilitator → All: It is now 07:40. Seven of nine cases have gone ahead or been moved. The ED is on diversion for ambulances. The forensic firm is on a call with the ISO. Overnight the hospital recorded 14 new admissions on paper, and the downtime packet on every unit is now four and a half hours old.
worldState: The hospital has been operating on paper for 4.5 hours.
Seven of nine scheduled surgical cases have proceeded or been rescheduled.
The ED remains on diversion for ambulance traffic.
The forensic firm is engaged and on a call with the ISO.
The downtime packet on every unit is now 4.5 hours old.
The EHR remains unavailable; no recovery steps have been initiated.
The EHR database servers ORRMC-SQL01 and ORRMC-SQL02 are isolated and offline.
The managed detection service continues to analyze the network for lateral movement.
fields.scenarioTitle: Paper Charts — EHR Downtime and Trust in the Record

instructorNote: This time jump establishes the operational strain of prolonged downtime. Watch for over-reliance on paper, fatigue in documentation, and pressure to resume EHR use prematurely.
